mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up our journey into radical self-love, let’s remind ourselves—this isn’t about reaching some finish line, or flipping a switch and never looking back. It’s about showing up, day after day, with a little more gentleness and a little more courage. Some days will feel easy, and others, not so much. But every step you take, every act of kindness toward yourself, matters more than you might realize. Here’s what stands out: Radical self-love is a practice, not a quick fix. We’re up against systems that try to make us feel less than, so healing becomes a collective act—one that’s about solidarity and lifting each other up. When we honor all the pieces of who we are—through intersectionality, compassion, and small, everyday choices—those ripples reach far beyond just ourselves. And setbacks? They’re part of the process. What matters is that you keep coming back, with persistence and a gentle hand. If you remember one thing, let it be this: you’re not alone. Your body isn’t a problem to solve. The world might try to tell you otherwise, but you have the power to write a new story—one where every act of self-love challenges old systems and brings us all closer to a world where every body is valued. You don’t have to get it perfect. You just have to start. Find your people, build your own practices, and know that healing is still possible—even on the toughest days. Your body isn’t an apology—it’s a miracle, a home, and a source of strength. Let that truth move you forward, and watch how it spreads out into the world. The revolution starts with you, but it doesn’t end here. Together, we can create something truly beautiful.
